species_event_concentration.interpretation: All nine Host+ first-record events are concentrated in four butterfly species; the temporal pattern is not broadly distributed across the panel.

decision.manuscript_use: Do not use Stage A as positive evidence that introduced-host placement predicts subsequent butterfly appearance.

ecological_interpretation: Static introduced-resource expansion does not translate into a detectable short-window placement effect on first documented butterfly occurrence once broad geography is preserved.

The result is compatible with temporal decoupling, dispersal limitation, habitat limitation, host-quality limitation, observation structure, or heterogeneous long lags; Stage A alone cannot distinguish these mechanisms.
A temporal-mismatch claim therefore requires an identity-specific host chronology test against matched non-host alien plants, not merely a butterfly time split.
claim_boundary: A first GBIF record is a first documented detection, not a colonization or establishment date.
Full-history correction removes cells with any focal-butterfly record through 2017 but cannot establish true biological absence.
Contemporary WCVP introduced ranges are time-invariant and do not establish host presence by 2017.

The full-protocol matched null is nearly degenerate for outcomes: only one mixed treatment/control stratum contains any events; species+Level1 is therefore the more informative geography-preserving null.
